extractedFacts.premisesPunitiveDamagesCap: $250,000 flat cap in most tort cases -- O.C.G.A. § 51-12-5.1(g) -- with NO cap where the case involves product liability, or the defendant acted with specific intent to cause harm or while impaired by drugs/alcohol. Held constitutional by the Georgia Supreme Court in 2023.
extractedFacts.premisesOpenAndObviousDoctrine: Traditional No-Duty Bar (operating through the 'equal/superior knowledge' rule rather than a separately labeled open-and-obvious doctrine)
extractedFacts.premisesOpenAndObviousCitation: Robinson v. Kroger Co., 268 Ga. 735, 493 S.E.2d 403 (Ga. 1997)
extractedFacts.premisesNegligentSecurityCitation: Georgia CVS Pharmacy, LLC v. Carmichael, 316 Ga. 718, 890 S.E.2d 209 (Ga. 2023)
extractedFacts.premisesLiabilityDistinctNote: Georgia draws a genuine, frequently litigated distinction between 'static condition' claims — governed by O.C.G.A. § 51-3-1's superior-knowledge, two-prong Robinson v. Kroger framework, where the owner's liability turns on knowledge superior to the plaintiff's — and 'active negligence' claims involving an owner's ongoing conduct, where the ordinary duty of care applies regardless of the plaintiff's own knowledge of the risk. This is conceptually similar to, though doctrinally distinct from, Texas's Keetch condition-versus-activity line, and correctly characterizing a claim as 'static condition' versus 'active negligence' is often outcome-determinative in Georgia premises litigation.

outcome.description: The jury returned a verdict of $1,718,367.46 in total damages, finding Khalia 66% at fault and the driver and the shooter 17% each; the trial court entered judgment against Khalia of approximately $1.134 million (66% of the verdict is $1,134,122.52), denied JNOV and new trial, and awarded Rosebud $140,951.17 in fees and expenses under OCGA 9-11-68 after Khalia rejected his $150,000 demand (Khalia's highest offer was $50,000). The Court of Appeals affirmed on December 6, 2019.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed. The opinion states the judgment only as approximately $1.134 million; the figure here is 66% of the stated verdict.
